ENFJ>INTJ.title: You work out plans for everyone, on your own.
ENFJ>INTJ.body: When a friend comes to you for advice, you listen first, then help them sort it out step by step: "Okay, so maybe try this." Thinking ahead and making plans has never changed for you. You like seeing people, but you also value your time alone to think.
ENFJ>INTJ.say: "I've worked out the flow. Tell me if anything doesn't work for you."
ENFJ>INTJ.do: When choosing where to move, you pick a neighborhood by thinking about your life five years from now.
ENFJ>INTJ.worry: The more efficient the plan, the more you worry it leaves someone's feelings behind, and you can't decide. The gap between days you want people and days you don't is big, and it throws you off too.
ENFJ>INTJ.karai: Once a trip is booked, you somehow know all the local restaurants before you even go.
ENFJ>INTJ.aru: When you're in charge of a welcome party, the prep is really fun. But on the day, as your turn for the toast gets closer, you suddenly want to go home.
ENFJ>INTJ.why: Thinking ahead and keeping things on plan is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you get energy from people and decide with your feelings. Along the way you learned to think things through alone and decide with logic. That's why your wish to see people comes in waves.
ENFJ>INTJ.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself in a meeting or picture yourself with friends, and your result can change.
ENFJ>INTJ.plus: You hesitate over efficient plans because you picture the people who might get left behind. Someone who builds a solid plan and still thinks of everyone makes a team feel safe.
ENFJ>INTJ.tip: When you share a plan, leave one part as "Let's decide this together." You don't have to decide it all alone, so it's easier to make up your mind.
ENFJ>INTJ.hidden: You often think with logic, but you were born good at noticing small changes in how people feel. When someone's voice gets a little quieter in a meeting, don't you right away ask, "What do you think?" Use that, and people will happily get on board with your plans.

ENFJ>INTP.title: You listen, and end up sorting out the cause too.
ENFJ>INTP.body: Looking at a painting in a museum, you wonder, "How was the artist feeling when they painted this?" Loving new things and "what if" ideas has never changed for you. You like talking with people, and you also like getting lost in thought alone.
ENFJ>INTP.say: "Wouldn't it be amazing if that actually worked?"
ENFJ>INTP.do: You look something up on your phone, and before you know it you're reading about something else entirely.
ENFJ>INTP.worry: You want to help people, and you also want to think about what interests you, so you're never sure how to spend your time. You can't move until your thoughts come together, but you keep thinking about the people you're keeping waiting.
ENFJ>INTP.karai: One news story, and you're worrying about things years down the road.
ENFJ>INTP.aru: When a friend says "I want to quit my part-time job," you listen, and somehow you're asking "What's the worst part?" and digging out the reasons. Even though you really want to cheer them up.
ENFJ>INTP.why: Loving new things and "what if" ideas is the same in your temperament and your type. Three things are different. By nature you get energy from people, decide with your feelings, and like to stick to a plan. Along the way you learned to think things over alone, check with logic, and wait and see instead of deciding. That's why, when you help someone, you end up looking for the cause.
ENFJ>INTP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. The question "Do you like to plan things out?" especially can flip depending on whether you picture yourself before a deadline or on a day off.
ENFJ>INTP.plus: Advice turns into looking for the cause because you really want to solve their problem. Someone who cheers you on and thinks it through with you is great to have.
ENFJ>INTP.tip: Before you talk about the cause, first just say, "That sounds really hard." After that, your thoughts will actually help them.
ENFJ>INTP.hidden: You often go with the flow, but you were also born good at getting ready ahead of time. The day before a trip, don't you check your bag again and again for anything you forgot? Use that for important plans and work, and people will feel safe leaving things to you.

ENFJ>ENTJ.title: You decide firmly, then quietly check on people.
ENFJ>ENTJ.body: You set the goal and lead everyone, and when someone can't keep up, you go talk to them. Getting energy from people, thinking ahead, and keeping things organized has never changed for you. You make clear calls with logic, but afterward you think about how people felt.
ENFJ>ENTJ.say: "How about the first Saturday of next month for the next meetup?"
ENFJ>ENTJ.do: On a trip with friends, you settle everything from where to go to the train home, right there with everyone.
ENFJ>ENTJ.worry: Even when you made the right call, at night you go over whether anyone got hurt. Even when you should be strict, one look at their face and you soften your words.
ENFJ>ENTJ.karai: Even in idle chat, you end up asking, "So who's doing what?"
ENFJ>ENTJ.aru: At club practice you say firmly, "Learn this song by next time." But on the train home, you remember the first-year who answered quietly and wonder whether to send them a message.
ENFJ>ENTJ.why: Getting energy from people, thinking ahead, and keeping things organized is the same in your temperament and your type. The only difference is how you decide. By nature you decide with your feelings, and along the way you learned to decide with logic. That's why you decide with logic by day, and at night you start thinking about how the other person feels.
ENFJ>ENTJ.yure: The only difference is logic or feelings. Picture yourself making a call at work and you lean toward logic. Picture a friend asking for advice and you lean toward feelings.
ENFJ>ENTJ.plus: You remember their face after deciding because you really pay attention to people. That's why people trust you even when you're strict.
ENFJ>ENTJ.tip: On days you say something strict, send a message that same day: "Sorry if I was too much. You always help so much." It clears your mind so you don't lie awake thinking about it.
ENFJ>ENTJ.hidden: You often decide with logic, but you were born good at noticing feelings people don't say. Don't you sometimes hear a friend's "I'm fine" and know from their voice they're actually tired? Use that, and people will feel really understood.

ENFJ>ENTP.title: You turn ideas no one else had into something everyone can do.
ENFJ>ENTP.body: In a discussion you say, "What if we flip it?" and come up with an idea nobody else thought of. Then you shape it so everyone can get on board. Getting energy from people and loving new ideas has never changed for you. You think about people's feelings, and you still push things through with logic.
ENFJ>ENTP.say: "Love that idea! Let's turn it into something we can all do."
ENFJ>ENTP.do: Chatting over dinner, you say "Let's all do this sometime!" and make a group chat right then.
ENFJ>ENTP.worry: You want to push your idea forward, but you also understand how the people against it feel, so you hit the brakes. Right after you make a plan, a more fun way pops up and you can't settle.
ENFJ>ENTP.karai: After disagreeing with someone's idea in a meeting, you message them, "It was a good idea though."
ENFJ>ENTP.aru: Right after you make a careful trip plan and send it to everyone, you're the one saying, "Actually, wouldn't this route be more fun?"
ENFJ>ENTP.why: Getting energy from people and being drawn to new ideas is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you decide with your feelings and feel safer with a plan made in advance. Along the way you learned to poke at things with logic and move toward whatever's more fun in the moment. That's why you want to improve even plans you made yourself.
ENFJ>ENTP.yure: The two differences are logic or feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself at a well-prepared event or picture yourself chatting with friends, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ENTP.plus: You want to change ideas because you always believe "We can make this more fun." That positive attitude has helped the people around you many times.
ENFJ>ENTP.tip: Before sending a plan to everyone, sleep on it for one night. If the new idea is good, it'll still be there in the morning, and you'll change plans after sending them less often.
ENFJ>ENTP.hidden: You're great at sharp comebacks, but you were also born good at knowing the words someone most needs to hear. When a friend is down, don't you say "You worked so hard" before you even think? Add a line like that in discussions, and even people who disagreed will listen to you.

ENFJ>INFJ.title: One-on-one, you really listen.
ENFJ>INFJ.body: In front of a group you cheer everyone on, and one-on-one you listen closely. You can gently put into words feelings the other person hasn't even noticed yet. Thinking ahead, caring about people's feelings, and keeping things on plan has never changed for you.
ENFJ>INFJ.say: "Before we all talk, tell me what you think first."
ENFJ>INFJ.do: The day before an important talk, you think about how the other person feels and decide what order to say things in.
ENFJ>INFJ.worry: The more you helped people that day, the more drained you are when you get home. You take in people's worries so deeply that your own heart gets heavy too.
ENFJ>INFJ.karai: You've already picked your friend's birthday present a month ahead.
ENFJ>INFJ.aru: You go out to eat with friends you haven't seen in a while, nodding and laughing along. On the way home you're suddenly exhausted, and even in bed you're still thinking about the worries you heard.
ENFJ>INFJ.why: Caring about people's feelings, thinking ahead, and keeping things on plan is the same in your temperament and your type. Only one thing is different. By nature you get energy from people, and along the way you learned to rest your feelings alone. That's why, after a lively time, you want some quiet.
ENFJ>INFJ.yure: The only difference is whether people energize you or you recharge alone. Picture your weekend or picture the day of a big get-together, and your result can change.
ENFJ>INFJ.plus: You're drained on the way home because you really gave your attention to each person there. Talking with people without holding back is one of your best qualities.
ENFJ>INFJ.tip: On days you see people, take 30 minutes after you get home to put your phone down and do nothing. Rest your body first, and you'll have energy to listen again.
ENFJ>INFJ.hidden: You value time alone to think, but you were born good at sorting out your thoughts by talking. Haven't you found the answer yourself while telling a friend about a worry? When you're stuck, talk to someone instead of carrying it alone, and you'll decide faster.

ENFJ>INFP.title: For other people, you move right away.
ENFJ>INFP.body: You jump into action for someone else, but for yourself, you take your time until you feel "This is it." Valuing ideas and people's feelings has never changed for you. You like being with people, but you also need time alone to sort out your feelings.
ENFJ>INFP.say: "I get how you feel. You can answer later, okay?"
ENFJ>INFP.do: Listening to a favorite song, you imagine, "Maybe this is about a breakup."
ENFJ>INFP.worry: You want to meet people's expectations and also be true to your own feelings, and you can't choose. Even with a plan, on days you're not in the mood you can't get started, and then you blame yourself.
ENFJ>INFP.karai: Just the movie trailer has you tearing up.
ENFJ>INFP.aru: When a friend changes jobs, you cheer them on with everything: "You've got this!" But your own class sign-up page has been sitting open for a week.
ENFJ>INFP.why: Valuing ideas and people's feelings is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you get energy from people and like to set the plan before you act. Along the way you started checking your feelings alone and going with the flow. That's why you move right away for others, but wait until your own feelings are settled for yourself.
ENFJ>INFP.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself helping someone or picture a day off alone, and your result can change.
ENFJ>INFP.plus: You hesitate about your own things because you don't want to do what you're not sure about. You take both other people's dreams and your own seriously.
ENFJ>INFP.tip: Tell a close friend in one line what you want to do. They'll ask "How's that going?", and it'll be easier to take the first step.
ENFJ>INFP.hidden: You like quiet time checking in with your feelings, but you were also born good at brightening a room. At a new get-together, don't you find yourself introducing people who don't know each other? Use that, and you'll fit in fast at a new job or class.

ENFJ>ENFJ.title: When you say "You've got this," you mean it.
ENFJ>ENFJ.body: When you say "It's okay, you can do it," you really believe it. Your temperament and type point the same way, so believing in people's good points, caring about their feelings, and helping everyone pull together have grown just as they are. Where you can be useful, you feel free and at ease, but where you can't see how people react, you tend to lose energy.
ENFJ>ENFJ.say: "It's okay, you can do this. Let's do it together!"
ENFJ>ENFJ.do: At a get-together full of strangers, you introduce people to each other, and by the time you leave you've made a group chat.
ENFJ>ENFJ.worry: When people ask, you take it all on, and your own time disappears. If the mood around you drops even a little, you wonder if it's your fault.
ENFJ>ENFJ.karai: When a friend asks for love advice, you make a game plan more seriously than they do.
ENFJ>ENFJ.aru: When someone in the group goes quiet, you worry "Did I say something?" and switch to a brighter topic.
ENFJ>ENFJ.why: Your temperament and type are the same in all four. Getting energy from people, believing in their good points, and bringing the group together with care have grown just as they are. You notice right away when the mood dips and jump in, because that strength is so strong in you.
ENFJ>ENFJ.yure: All four line up, so you tend to get the same result no matter how many times you take it. If you get a different one, you may be carrying too many favors and wanting to be alone more than usual.
ENFJ>ENFJ.plus: You notice changes in the mood right away, so no one ends up left out when you're around. That's not overthinking. It's how much you care about everyone.
ENFJ>ENFJ.tip: When someone goes quiet, pause for a breath before changing the subject. Asking later, "Were you okay back there?" is easier on both of you.
ENFJ>ENFJ.hidden: You're great at sticking to the plan, but you also have a not-yet-used "enjoy the moment" side. Has a shop you wandered into on a day when plans fell apart ever become your best memory? Use that, and you can laugh easily even when things don't go as planned.

ENFJ>ENFP.title: You make the plan, and still enjoy the detours.
ENFJ>ENFP.body: In your trip schedule, you leave a block marked "free time" on purpose. Getting energy from people and valuing ideas and people's feelings has never changed for you. You're good at making plans, and you also enjoy changing them on the spot.
ENFJ>ENFP.say: "Hey, want to all go to the beach on our next day off?"
ENFJ>ENFP.do: You plan the birthday party carefully, and on the day you jump right into a game someone just made up.
ENFJ>ENFP.worry: You want people to be happy, so you pack the schedule, and then you have no free time for yourself. The gap between days you want order and days you don't want to decide anything throws you off.
ENFJ>ENFP.karai: You call saying "Let's talk for a sec," and it's never just a sec.
ENFJ>ENFP.aru: On a trip with friends, you looked up and saved every place you wanted to go, but on the day you're the first to say, "Want to try that side street?"
ENFJ>ENFP.why: Getting energy from people and valuing ideas and people's feelings is the same in your temperament and your type. The only difference is how you move forward. By nature you like to make a plan first, and along the way you also learned to go with the moment. That's why you can do your research and still take all the detours you want.
ENFJ>ENFP.yure: The only difference is sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture work or getting ready and you lean toward planning. Picture having fun and you lean toward going with the flow.
ENFJ>ENFP.plus: You pack the schedule because you want everyone to say "That was fun." Someone who enjoys both the prep and the detours is never boring to be with.
ENFJ>ENFP.tip: When you plan a day, decide just half of it and leave the rest open. That open time often turns into the best memory.
ENFJ>ENFP.hidden: You can enjoy going with the flow, but you were born good at finishing things properly. Don't you sometimes find you've wrapped up a task alone after everyone else got bored and stopped? Use that at work, and people will see you as both fun and reliable.

ENFJ>ISTJ.title: You follow the rules so no one gets stuck.
ENFJ>ISTJ.body: Before you share a document everyone will use, you check it again and again so anyone can follow it. People see you as "so organized," but really you just don't want anyone to get stuck. Following through on what you decide has never changed for you.
ENFJ>ISTJ.say: "Could you have this done by Friday?"
ENFJ>ISTJ.do: Before a trip, you check the weather and train times and send them to everyone.
ENFJ>ISTJ.worry: You want people to follow the rules, but you don't want to blame them, so you struggle with how to point things out. You want to see people, but if you're not ready, you're tired before you even meet.
ENFJ>ISTJ.karai: You arrive ten minutes early and are already messaging the friend who's running late.
ENFJ>ISTJ.aru: Writing a message to tell a junior about a mistake, you reread it again and again to make sure it doesn't sound harsh, and end up rewriting it three times.
ENFJ>ISTJ.why: Wanting to keep things neatly on plan is the same in your temperament and your type. Three things are different. By nature you get energy from people, imagine what's ahead, and decide with your feelings. Along the way you learned to focus alone, build on facts, and decide with logic. That's why you want to say it correctly and kindly, and keep rewriting.
ENFJ>ISTJ.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself following procedures at work or picture yourself with friends you get along with, and a different type may come up.
ENFJ>ISTJ.plus: Because you take such care with your words, people think, "If they say so, I'll listen." Someone who cares about both the rules and people's feelings is someone the office relies on.
ENFJ>ISTJ.tip: When you need to point something out, decide to always send it in this order: what happened, what you'd like, and thanks. It won't sound harsh, so you can send it without rereading it over and over.
ENFJ>ISTJ.hidden: You build on facts one by one, but you were born good at imagining what's ahead. While working, don't you sometimes think, "This could be better if..."? Say it out loud, and people at work will rely on you even more.

ENFJ>ISFJ.title: You notice right away when someone's not feeling well.
ENFJ>ISFJ.body: This person doesn't like spicy food, that one was coughing a bit yesterday. You just remember things like that. Caring about people's feelings and keeping things on plan has never changed for you. In front of everyone you cheer people on, and behind the scenes you take care of the little things.
ENFJ>ISFJ.say: "You were coughing a little yesterday, right? I brought you throat drops."
ENFJ>ISFJ.do: When you organize a farewell party, you book a place that serves the food the guest of honor once said they loved.
ENFJ>ISFJ.worry: Doing things for others doesn't bother you, but your own plans always come last. Some days you want to talk about big dreams, but you stop yourself: "I need to be realistic."
ENFJ>ISFJ.karai: You say "Don't worry about me," and you're the one worrying about everyone the most.
ENFJ>ISFJ.aru: You start telling a friend, "Someday I want to open a shop," and halfway through you end it yourself: "Well, it's not realistic though."
ENFJ>ISFJ.why: Caring about people's feelings and preparing well is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you get energy from people and imagine what's ahead. Along the way you learned to settle down alone and check the facts in front of you. That's why, even when you start talking about a dream, you end up looking at reality halfway through.
ENFJ>ISFJ.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and hunches or facts. Picture yourself at a lively celebration or picture yourself doing daily chores and work, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ISFJ.plus: You can talk about your dreams and still keep your feet on the ground. People like that can make what they want happen, little by little.
ENFJ>ISFJ.tip: Instead of ending your dream talk with "But it's impossible," try ending with "So what could I do first?" When it ends on a positive note, the people listening will share ideas too.
ENFJ>ISFJ.hidden: You value quiet time alone, but you were born good at bringing people together and livening things up. When a friend you haven't seen in a while comes to mind, don't you say, "Want to get together?" Use that, and your circle of people will keep growing.

ENFJ>ESTJ.title: You're strict, but you always give credit.
ENFJ>ESTJ.body: While you check how the work is going, you also praise the team's small wins. People like you even though you're strict, because you really notice their effort. Getting energy from people and setting a plan to move forward has never changed for you.
ENFJ>ESTJ.say: "Let's finish by the end of the month. This team can do it."
ENFJ>ESTJ.do: At work drinks, you set the ending time so everyone can catch the last train.
ENFJ>ESTJ.worry: Every time, you're torn between speaking up to someone who breaks the rules and thinking about their feelings. The more you focus on reality, the further you feel from the dreams you used to have.
ENFJ>ESTJ.karai: You manage the team's schedule perfectly, but your own break is always "if there's time."
ENFJ>ESTJ.aru: You can tell a late coworker plainly, "Please be on time," but the whole way home you keep wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
ENFJ>ESTJ.why: Getting energy from people and keeping things neatly on plan is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you imagine future dreams and decide with your feelings. Along the way you learned to look at the facts in front of you and decide with logic. That's why, after you point something out, you worry about how they feel.
ENFJ>ESTJ.yure: The two differences are hunches or facts, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself on the job or picture time with people close to you, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ESTJ.plus: You worry about how you said it because you're thinking about that person's future too. The care behind your strictness does reach them.
ENFJ>ESTJ.tip: After pointing something out, end by telling them one thing they did well. It won't end on harsh words, so you'll worry less on the way home.
ENFJ>ESTJ.hidden: You act on the facts in front of you, but you were born good at imagining years ahead. On the way home from work, don't you sometimes get excited thinking, "In a few years I'd like to change how we do this"? Share that with your team, and it'll be easier for everyone to have a goal.

ENFJ>ESFJ.title: You can't help taking care of everyone.
ENFJ>ESFJ.body: Right after pitching a big idea for next year, you ask, "Did everyone eat lunch?" That's why you're the center of calm at any gathering. Drawing energy from people, caring about feelings and moving with a plan has always been your core. A feel for what can't be seen yet and a respect for experience and facts each show up when needed.
ENFJ>ESFJ.say: "You haven't had lunch yet, right? I got extra rice balls."
ENFJ>ESFJ.do: You volunteer to help run a school or work event, and on the day you walk around checking that everyone's having fun.
ENFJ>ESFJ.worry: You want everyone to be happy so badly that one unhappy face keeps your heart from resting. You're pulled both by wanting to try new things and by wanting to protect the way things work.
ENFJ>ESFJ.karai: While you're serving food to everyone, yours goes cold.
ENFJ>ESFJ.aru: You said "This year I want to try new things," but when it's time to pick a restaurant, you end up at the usual place.
ENFJ>ESFJ.why: Getting energy from people, caring about feelings, and keeping things organized are steady parts where your temperament and character line up. The only difference is where you look. By temperament, you dream about possibilities, and through experience you learned to pay close attention to the people and facts right in front of you. You're drawn to both newness and comfort because you have both ways of seeing.
ENFJ>ESFJ.yure: Only one tendency differs: future possibilities or present facts. Picture yourself talking about the future and you lean on inspiration; picture yourself doing chores or preparing an event and you lean practical, so you may go back and forth between two types.
ENFJ>ESFJ.plus: You get excited about new things and still choose places where everyone feels at ease. People who value both dreams and comfort are the ones others rely on.
ENFJ>ESFJ.tip: At your usual place, try ordering just one new dish. Small "firsts" add up and make bigger new steps easier.
ENFJ>ESFJ.hidden: You pay close attention to the people in front of you, and your temperament also lets you see what they could become. When you tell a friend or junior coworker, "I think you'd be great at this," and you turn out to be right, that strength is at work. Use it on purpose, and you'll become the trusted mentor who helps others grow.

ENFJ>ISTP.title: Your hands move before your words.
ENFJ>ISTP.body: You don't say much, you just quickly take care of the problem in front of you. But inside, you want to cheer the people around you on. Your temperament and type differ in all four, so you can do a wide range of things.
ENFJ>ISTP.say: "Eh, it'll work out. Don't overthink it."
ENFJ>ISTP.do: When your bike chain comes off, you stay calm and fix it right there.
ENFJ>ISTP.worry: You want to encourage people, but it feels awkward, so you tend to let your actions do the talking. You do so much for others that you run out of time for yourself.
ENFJ>ISTP.karai: The topic you said you're "not that into" is the one you secretly look up once you get home.
ENFJ>ISTP.aru: When a junior is down, you quietly help with their work before you say anything. At home you think, "I should have said something more."
ENFJ>ISTP.why: Your temperament and type are different in all four. By nature you get energy from people, imagine what's ahead, decide with your feelings, and like to stick to a plan. Along the way you learned to focus alone, look at the facts, think with logic, and get your hands moving on the spot. That's why you show your warm feelings through action more than words.
ENFJ>ISTP.yure: All four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself quietly working or picture yourself cheering on your friends, and you might get a completely different type.
ENFJ>ISTP.plus: Even without words, your quiet help really reaches people. Feeling awkward means you care about them.
ENFJ>ISTP.tip: After you help, add just one line: "Don't push yourself." A short line sounds more like you than a long speech.
ENFJ>ISTP.hidden: You look at facts and think with logic, but you were born good at imagining what's ahead. While using your phone or appliances, don't you sometimes think, "It'd be so handy if it had this feature"? Say that at work, and it can turn into ideas that help people.

ENFJ>ISFP.title: You can't help buying things that would suit your friends.
ENFJ>ISFP.body: Words that cheer everyone up, a small gift you picked out alone: you give both naturally. Deciding with people's feelings in mind has never changed for you. Sometimes going with your mood that day is easier than making a plan.
ENFJ>ISFP.say: "Hey, isn't this color cute? Look, look!"
ENFJ>ISFP.do: You keep changing up your room a little with seasonal flowers and small things.
ENFJ>ISFP.worry: The more you plan to meet people's expectations, the less your heart keeps up. You love lively places, but afterward you can't feel like yourself again without quiet time alone.
ENFJ>ISFP.karai: You get so into prepping the party that you're already sleepy the morning of.
ENFJ>ISFP.aru: For a friend's birthday, you go all out and even make homemade sweets. But once the party's over, you soak in the bath alone and can't move for a while.
ENFJ>ISFP.why: Deciding with people's feelings in mind is the same in your temperament and your type. Three things are different. By nature you get energy from people, think ahead, and like to stick to a plan. Along the way you learned to rest alone, enjoy what's in front of you, and follow your mood. That's why, after going all out, you need quiet time alone.
ENFJ>ISFP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself running an event or picture a lazy day off, and a different type may come up.
ENFJ>ISFP.plus: You notice you're tired late because you think about the other person's feelings first. Turning what makes people happy into something real is one of your best qualities.
ENFJ>ISFP.tip: Keep the day after a fun event completely free. If you know when you'll rest, you won't let tiredness pile up.
ENFJ>ISFP.hidden: You're good at enjoying what's in front of you, but you were also born good at dreaming big about what's ahead. When you see a view you love, don't thoughts like "Someday I want to do this" start to spread? Tell a close friend about that dream, and your "Maybe I'll try it" will grow stronger.

ENFJ>ESTP.title: Once it comes up, you book it on the spot.
ENFJ>ESTP.body: When a friend tells you their problem, you immediately reach out: "Let's ask so-and-so about that." Getting energy from people has never changed for you. More often than not, you try things first instead of thinking ahead.
ENFJ>ESTP.say: "Okay, I'll call the restaurant right now and ask."
ENFJ>ESTP.do: Even at a shop you don't know, if it catches your eye, you just walk in.
ENFJ>ESTP.worry: After deciding on impulse, you wonder if anyone got left behind. Part of you wants to plan carefully, but in the end you're thinking while you run.
ENFJ>ESTP.karai: Thirty minutes after texting "Free?", you're already meeting someone at the station.
ENFJ>ESTP.aru: A friend says "Someday I want to go there," and you say "Then let's go this weekend!" and book it right then. On the way home you think, "Was I a bit pushy?"
ENFJ>ESTP.why: Getting energy from people is the same in your temperament and your type. Three things are different. By nature you think ahead, decide with people's feelings in mind, and plan carefully. Along the way you learned to grab the chance in front of you, decide quickly with logic, and act right away. That's why, after you charge ahead, you look back on how everyone felt.
ENFJ>ESTP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself heading out on a whim on your day off or picture yourself helping someone close to you, and a different type may come up.
ENFJ>ESTP.plus: You look back after acting because you care about people. Someone with energy who also looks out for others is fun to be with.
ENFJ>ESTP.tip: When you want to decide right away, ask once, "What do you all think?" before booking. That alone means a lot less worrying on the way home.
ENFJ>ESTP.hidden: You're good at grabbing the chance in front of you, but you were born good at thinking ahead too. While planning an outing, don't you sometimes think, "This will be a great memory for everyone"? Say that before you act, and people will be happy to come along.

ENFJ>ESFP.title: When everyone's together, you're the most excited one there.
ENFJ>ESFP.body: When you go out, you take photos and come up with games to get everyone going. Getting energy from people and deciding with your feelings has never changed for you. You do think ahead, but you're better at enjoying right now.
ENFJ>ESFP.say: "Let's forget everything bad today and just have fun together!"
ENFJ>ESFP.do: You planned your friend's celebration, but on the day you're the most excited one there.
ENFJ>ESFP.worry: You want to treasure the fun, but thinking about the future suddenly makes you anxious. You get so caught up in making people happy that your real feelings come last.
ENFJ>ESFP.karai: You cry and laugh with your friends, and by the time you head home your voice is gone.
ENFJ>ESFP.aru: After getting fired up helping a friend with their future plans, you say "Okay, let's sing!" and go straight to karaoke. At home you look at this month's spending and panic.
ENFJ>ESFP.why: Getting energy from people and deciding with your feelings is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you dream about the future and like to stick to a plan. Along the way you learned to enjoy the moment to the fullest and go with the flow. That's why, even right after a talk about the future, you can jump into having fun.
ENFJ>ESFP.yure: The two differences are hunches or facts, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Whether you're in a stretch of working toward a goal or a stretch full of fun plans can change your result.
ENFJ>ESFP.plus: You get fired up about the future and still laugh with everything you've got today. Being around you gives people energy.
ENFJ>ESFP.tip: Before you go out, decide "I'll spend up to this much today." Inside that limit you can just enjoy yourself, and you won't panic when you get home.
ENFJ>ESFP.hidden: You're good at going with the flow, but you were also born good at getting things in order. On days everyone goes out together, don't you find yourself sending out the meeting time and what to bring? Use that, and people will see you as fun and reliable.

ENFP>INTJ.title: When you get an idea, you start planning that same day.
ENFP>INTJ.body: You don't leave an exciting idea as just an idea. Before you know it, you've made a detailed plan on your own. Loving new things and thinking about what's ahead has never changed for you. You like having fun with people, but you also value time alone to think things through.
ENFP>INTJ.say: "Doesn't this idea seem doable? I looked into it a little."
ENFP>INTJ.do: You start a hobby on a whim, look it up through videos and books, and end up knowing more than anyone around you.
ENFP>INTJ.worry: Ideas come in a flash, but you try to make the plan perfect, so it takes a while to get started. The gap between days you want to hang out and days you don't want to see anyone is big.
ENFP>INTJ.karai: Right after getting an idea, you're already looking for what's wrong with it.
ENFP>INTJ.aru: The night you think "I want to open a café!", you look up startup costs alone until late. When a friend asks "So when are you starting?", you don't know what to say.
ENFP>INTJ.why: Being drawn to new things and what's ahead is the same in your temperament and your type. Three things are different. By nature you get energy from having fun with people, decide with your feelings, and move freely. Along the way you learned to think alone, decide with logic, and make plans. That's why your ideas turn into plans so fast.
ENFP>INTJ.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself trading ideas with friends or picture yourself working out a plan alone, and a different type may come up.
ENFP>INTJ.plus: Planning takes time because you really mean to make your ideas happen. Surprisingly few people do more than just talk.
ENFP>INTJ.tip: When your plan is about 70% done, tell one person about it first. You'll get feedback and feel like you've already started, so you won't get stuck overthinking.
ENFP>INTJ.hidden: You often think things through alone, but you were born good at getting close to people you've just met. Even when you don't know anyone, don't you end up in the middle of the laughing group? Share your plans with people, and helpers will gather naturally.

ENFP>INTP.title: Once you wonder "why?", you can't stop.
ENFP>INTP.body: An old building you spotted on a walk catches your interest, and back home you look up even the year it was built. Valuing your ideas and going with the flow has never changed for you. You like growing ideas by talking with people, and you also like digging into how things work alone.
ENFP>INTP.say: "This is fun. But why is it so fun?"
ENFP>INTP.do: At a bookstore you come home with a pile of books that caught your eye, whatever the genre.
ENFP>INTP.worry: Your interests keep jumping, so you rarely feel you've finished anything. After saying something logically right, you worry you left the other person's feelings behind.
ENFP>INTP.karai: The things you've decided to "start tomorrow" keep piling up.
ENFP>INTP.aru: Chatting with a friend, you wonder "Why do cats love boxes?", and back home you look it up until late. The next day you bring it up, and your friend has already forgotten.
ENFP>INTP.why: Following your ideas and going with the flow is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you get energy from having fun with people and decide with your feelings. Along the way you learned to dig into how things work alone and think with logic. That's why you want to look up everything later about what you talked about with people.
ENFP>INTP.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself at a lively party or picture yourself researching alone, and your result can change.
ENFP>INTP.plus: Your interests jump around because you notice so many interesting things. What you learn doesn't disappear. Someday it connects with something else and turns out useful.
ENFP>INTP.tip: Send a friend a quick line about what you found out that same day. Telling someone gives it an ending, so you'll feel you saw it through.
ENFP>INTP.hidden: You love thinking with logic, but you were also born good at sensing how people feel. When a friend is down, don't you sometimes think, "I'll just listen for now," before giving any answer? Use that, and what you know will really reach people.

ENFP>ENTJ.title: You start things for fun, and actually get them done.
ENFP>ENTJ.body: You talk about something exciting, then right away assign who does what and set the deadline. It's the speed that surprises people. Getting energy from people and valuing your ideas has never changed for you.
ENFP>ENTJ.say: "Let's all do it! Let's pick who does what and get it done by the end of the month."
ENFP>ENTJ.do: When there's a concert you want to see, you put the ticket release date on your calendar and invite your friends too.
ENFP>ENTJ.worry: The harder you push for results, the fewer happy faces you seem to see. You want to stick to the plan, and you also want to take the fun detours.
ENFP>ENTJ.karai: The one who said "Let's keep it fun" is the one most serious about winning.
ENFP>ENTJ.aru: You were the one who said "Let's make the club trip fun!", but somehow you've planned every detail and are a bit irritated with people running late.
ENFP>ENTJ.why: Getting energy from people and valuing your ideas is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you decide with your feelings and move freely. Along the way you learned to decide with logic, set up the steps, and get results. That's why you want both fun and results.
ENFP>ENTJ.yure: The two differences are logic or feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a stretch of chasing goals at work or picture your day off, and your result can change.
ENFP>ENTJ.plus: You feel down when faces cloud over because you care about having fun together, not only results. People gather around a leader like that.
ENFP>ENTJ.tip: When you make a schedule, add one block of free time with nothing planned. If things run late, you can catch up there, and you'll enjoy it too instead of getting irritated.
ENFP>ENTJ.hidden: You often decide with logic, but you were born good at choosing your words with people's feelings in mind. With a teammate who seems down, don't you say "Thanks for always being here" before talking strategy? Use that, and people will think, "I want to work hard with this person."

ENFP>ENTP.title: You can't help asking, "Can that really work?"
ENFP>ENTP.body: You don't just come up with ideas. You ask both "Who will this make happy?" and "Will this actually work?" Spotting fun things fast and acting on the spot has never changed for you. You poke at things with logic, but you also pay attention to how people feel.
ENFP>ENTP.say: "That's fun! But let's check if there's anywhere it could go wrong."
ENFP>ENTP.do: Helping a friend with a problem, halfway through you've come up with three "What if you tried this?" ideas.
ENFP>ENTP.worry: After winning an argument, you remember the other person's face and feel down. Every time, you're torn between saying what's right and saying it kindly.
ENFP>ENTP.karai: The chat gets so lively that nobody remembers what you were talking about in the first place.
ENFP>ENTP.aru: When a friend shares what they thought of a movie, you can't help saying, "But didn't that part not make sense?" When they go quiet, you rush to add, "No, I liked some scenes too!"
ENFP>ENTP.why: Getting energy from people, being drawn to new ideas, and going with the flow is the same in your temperament and your type. The only difference is how you decide. By nature you decide with your feelings, and along the way you learned to think with logic. That's why, after you poke at something, you worry about how they feel.
ENFP>ENTP.yure: The only difference is logic or feelings. Picture a lively discussion and you lean toward logic. Picture cheering up a friend who's down and you lean toward feelings.
ENFP>ENTP.plus: You feel down after poking at things because you're really watching the other person's face. People listen to someone who doesn't leave others behind just to be right.
ENFP>ENTP.tip: When you want to point something out, say one thing you liked first. Just changing the order makes the same point land more gently.
ENFP>ENTP.hidden: You're good at poking holes with logic, but you were born good at sharing in what other people love. When a friend talks about something they love, don't you find their happy face makes you happier than the topic itself? Tell them that, and they'll feel, "It's fun being with this person."

ENFP>INFJ.title: You remember the little things people say in passing.
ENFP>INFJ.body: You make friends with anyone fast, and you really listen to what they say. Thinking about new things and deciding with people's feelings in mind has never changed for you. After a lively time with people, you want some quiet alone.
ENFP>INFJ.say: "Oh, that's lovely! What do you like about it?"
ENFP>INFJ.do: You remember something a person mentioned in passing, and a few days later you ask, "Hey, did that turn out okay?"
ENFP>INFJ.worry: You want to act on ideas right away, but you stop and wonder, "Is this right?" You like seeing people, but after a deep talk you need time alone.
ENFP>INFJ.karai: Once your favorite artist comes up, you start sharing memories nobody asked for.
ENFP>INFJ.aru: You hit it off with someone new and swap contact info, but at home you put your phone face down: "I don't want to talk to anyone else today."
ENFP>INFJ.why: Thinking about new things and deciding with people's feelings in mind is the same in your temperament and your type. Two things are different. By nature you get energy from people and follow your mood. Along the way you learned to rest alone and work steadily toward goals. That's why, after getting close to people, you want to be alone.
ENFP>INFJ.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself out with friends or picture yourself working on an important goal, and your result can change.
ENFP>INFJ.plus: You get close to people fast because you really pay attention to the person in front of you. It's natural to be tired after that.
ENFP>INFJ.tip: On nights after seeing people, it's fine to put your phone down and rest. Send "Yesterday was fun" the next morning, and they'll get the message.
ENFP>INFJ.hidden: You work steadily toward your goals, but you were born good at enjoying the unexpected. Have you ever gotten off at a random station when the train stopped and been happy to find a great shop? Use that, and even days that don't go to plan can be fun.

ENFP>INFP.title: You say "I'm in!" and then waver the night before.
ENFP>INFP.body: In a lively group your voice is the loudest, but in your time alone you go back over what you felt. Valuing your ideas, deciding with your feelings, and following your mood has never changed for you. You like seeing people, but you need time alone just as much.
ENFP>INFP.say: "I totally get that feeling. I was thinking the same thing."
ENFP>INFP.do: The day after a big hangout, you don't contact anyone and spend the day at home watching your favorite videos.
ENFP>INFP.worry: Your waves between wanting people and wanting to be alone are big, so some days you feel heavy after agreeing to plans. You love lots of things, but you tend to move on before any of them take shape.
ENFP>INFP.karai: Every time you watch a moving video, you say, "This changed my life."
ENFP>INFP.aru: You answered "I'm in!" right away for the weekend get-together, but the night before, it suddenly feels like a hassle. Then you go, have the most fun of anyone, and replay it alone on the train home.
ENFP>INFP.why: Valuing your ideas, deciding with your feelings, and following your mood is the same in your temperament and your type. Only one thing is different. By nature you get energy from people, and along the way you also learned to recharge with time alone. That's why you jump at invitations and then waver the night before.
ENFP>INFP.yure: The only difference is whether people energize you or you recharge alone. Think of a recent day out or think of a quiet day at home, and your result can change.
ENFP>INFP.plus: Even if you feel heavy the day before, once you go you really enjoy it. That's because you care about both your connections and your own time.
ENFP>INFP.tip: When you accept an invite, say up front, "I want to come! I might leave early though." Just knowing you can leave anytime makes the night before feel lighter.
ENFP>INFP.hidden: You recharge with time alone, but you were born good at growing ideas the more you talk. Haven't you been chatting with a friend and suddenly decided, "Let's do that together!"? Make a habit of telling someone your ideas, and the things you want to do will take shape faster.

ENFP>ENFJ.title: When you suggest something, you see it through.
ENFP>ENFJ.body: A surprise you thought up on a whim, you actually pull off that same day by lining up everyone's schedules. Getting energy from people and valuing ideas and people's feelings has never changed for you. You don't stop at suggesting things, so you end up at the center of the group.
ENFP>ENFJ.say: "That sounds fun! It'll be even more fun if we all do it."
ENFP>ENFJ.do: When someone new joins, you go talk to them first and bring them into the group.
ENFP>ENFJ.worry: The more you're put in charge, the less time you have to act on a whim. You feel so responsible that you hold on to plans even on days you're not in the mood.
ENFP>ENFJ.karai: You meant to cheer up your friend, and somehow you're the one crying.
ENFP>ENFJ.aru: You say "I want to go camping with everyone," and somehow you end up handling the booking and messages. On the day, watching your friends play freely, you feel a little jealous.
ENFP>ENFJ.why: Getting energy from people and valuing ideas and people's feelings is the same in your temperament and your type. The only difference is how you move forward. By nature you like to move freely, and along the way you learned to think ahead and see things through. That's why the things you suggest end up being organized by you.
ENFP>ENFJ.yure: The only difference is sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself organizing an event and you lean toward planning. Picture a day off wandering around and you lean toward going with the flow.
ENFP>ENFJ.plus: You hold on to plans because you want to take care of what you started until the end. You take responsibility for your ideas, so people feel safe following you.
ENFP>ENFJ.tip: When you're in charge, hand just one job for the day to someone else. Decide "During this time, I get to play too," and you'll enjoy it as well.
ENFP>ENFJ.hidden: You're often trusted with the planning, but you were born good at finding new ways to have fun when plans change. When rain canceled your outing, haven't you switched right away to "Okay, let's watch movies at home!"? Use that, and you can stay calm whatever happens.

ENFP>ENFP.title: You find the fun stuff fast.
ENFP>ENFP.body: Getting off at a station you don't know and walking into a shop that catches your eye: days like that suit you. Your temperament and type point the same way, so getting excited about new things, believing in people's good points, and trying whatever you feel like have grown just as they are. In places where you can move freely you thrive, but in places full of rules and repetition, you tend to lose energy.
ENFP>ENFP.say: "Wait, that sounds fun! Let's go check it out!"
ENFP>ENFP.do: You see a new shop on social media and invite a friend to go that same day.
ENFP>ENFP.worry: You love starting things, but you blame yourself when they don't last. You seem cheerful, but sometimes a passing comment hurts you deeply.
ENFP>ENFP.karai: You have tons of things you want to do, and only a few you've actually finished.
ENFP>ENFP.aru: Every time you start a new hobby you buy all the gear, and three months later you're into something else. Your closet is filling up with stuff you don't use anymore.
ENFP>ENFP.why: Your temperament and type are the same in all four. Getting energy from people, riding your ideas, deciding with your feelings, and moving lightly have grown just as they are. You keep jumping into new things because that sense of excitement is so strong in you.
ENFP>ENFP.yure: All four line up, so you tend to get the same result every time. If you get a different one, you may be pushing hard somewhere with lots of rules, or your energy may be a bit low.
ENFP>ENFP.plus: You blame yourself for not sticking with things, but not many people have the nerve to start. From all you've tried, you have a pile of fun stories to tell.
ENFP>ENFP.tip: Instead of "It's a success if it lasts," try thinking "It's a success if I enjoyed it once." Even hobbies you quit stay with you as good memories.
ENFP>ENFP.hidden: You love lively places, but you also have a not-yet-used "think it over alone" side. After a movie you love, isn't there a night when you'd rather not talk to anyone and just go over it alone for a while? Use that, and among all the things you love, you'll find the ones you want to keep doing.

ENFP>ISTJ.title: So proper, and so surprisingly fun to talk to.
ENFP>ISTJ.body: The report is done right on deadline, yet there's a little playful touch hiding on the last page. The sincerity to do what's decided with precision lives side by side with a curiosity that lights up at new possibilities. Focus alone and fun with others, an eye for facts and a heart for feelings, keeping plans and acting on a whim — you have all of them.
ENFP>ISTJ.say: "Let's stick to the usual steps. It's faster that way."
ENFP>ISTJ.do: You always put your keys and phone in the same spot by the door.
ENFP>ISTJ.worry: You get everything done properly, yet when every day feels the same, something seems missing. You want to try your ideas, but "What if it fails?" makes you overly careful.
ENFP>ISTJ.karai: You sit through the meeting with a serious face while planning your weekend fun in your head.
ENFP>ISTJ.aru: At work you're known as "the meticulous one," and you've never missed a deadline. But when every day starts to look the same, you get restless and want to hop off at a station you've never been to.
ENFP>ISTJ.why: By temperament, you get excited with people, chase new ideas, decide by feelings, and move lightly. Through experience, you learned to focus alone, check the facts, judge by logic, and stick to the plan. Because all four differ, you have both a steady routine and a hunger for adventure. Both are part of who you are.
ENFP>ISTJ.yure: All four tendencies differ, so your results can change a lot each time. Picture yourself at work and you come out steady and meticulous; picture yourself traveling and you come out a free adventurer, so the results can look completely different.
ENFP>ISTJ.plus: You feel that restlessness because part of you is always looking for something new and fun. With both caution and curiosity, you can keep up new things without strain.
ENFP>ISTJ.tip: Once a month, pick a day to stop by a shop or station you've never been to. When it's already on the schedule, even careful you can relax and enjoy a small adventure.
ENFP>ISTJ.hidden: People trust you for being meticulous, but your temperament also lets you warm someone's heart in an instant. When you can't help adding "You're always such a help!" at the end of a work message, that's this strength. Use it on purpose, and "the precise one" becomes "the one everyone wants to work with."

ENFP>ISFJ.title: A fun idea, with a rainy-day plan attached.
ENFP>ISFJ.body: When you think of a picnic, you look up a rainy-day spot too, just in case. Even with fun plans, you check "Is everyone okay?" before you move. Deciding with your heart is the part of you that stays the same. Energy from people and calm alone, an eye for the new and care with facts, lightness and loyalty — you have both of each.
ENFP>ISFJ.say: "Sounds fun! But let's pick a day she can come too."
ENFP>ISFJ.do: You're tempted to pick a bold gift for a friend, but in the end you carefully choose something they'll really use.
ENFP>ISFJ.worry: You want to dive into new things, but worrying about bothering others keeps you from taking the step. When asked, you say yes, and your own fun gets pushed back.
ENFP>ISFJ.karai: Full of the urge for adventure — and ordering the usual, at the usual place.
ENFP>ISFJ.aru: A friend says "Let's take a trip abroad together!" and in your head you're already going. But what comes out of your mouth is "I wonder if I can get time off..."
ENFP>ISFJ.why: Deciding with people's feelings in mind is the steady part your temperament and character share. By temperament, you light up around people, jump into new things, and move freely. Through experience you learned to settle down alone, check the facts carefully, and prepare properly. Excitement and worry show up together because you have both a sense of adventure and consideration for others.
ENFP>ISFJ.yure: Three tendencies differ, so your results can change a lot. You may wobble most on "Do you like new things?" and "Do you plan ahead?" depending on whether you picture a trip or your everyday work.
ENFP>ISFJ.plus: You can't take the first step because you don't want your fun to cause anyone trouble. That kindness is why people around you cheer on your adventures.
ENFP>ISFJ.tip: Start new things small: "just look it up" or "go once." A small step won't trouble anyone, so you can take it without worrying.
ENFP>ISFJ.hidden: People may see you as reserved, but your temperament also gives you the power to light up a group. When you're with close friends and realize you're the one making everyone laugh the most, that's this strength. Try using a little of it with new people too, and your circle will grow a lot.

ENFP>ESTJ.title: Tight on plans, generous with play.
ENFP>ESTJ.body: You set the plan and lead the way, while slipping in little detours that brighten the room. A fun kind of organizer. Drawing energy from people is your steady core. Imagination and real-world follow-through, heart and logic, freedom and sticking to the plan — you have both of each.
ENFP>ESTJ.say: "We meet at nine. If you're running late, let me know early."
ENFP>ESTJ.do: You set out exactly how the work will go, but open each meeting with a funny story from your week.
ENFP>ESTJ.worry: The more responsibility you're given, the more you feel you're forgetting the joy of acting on a whim. After calling someone out by the rules, you can't stop wondering if they're feeling down.
ENFP>ESTJ.karai: Five minutes after saying "Let's play it by ear," you're sending everyone a detailed plan.
ENFP>ESTJ.aru: You firmly tell a junior, "Please follow the steps," then can't stop glancing over to check they're not struggling.
ENFP>ESTJ.why: Getting energy from people is the one part that hasn't changed. By temperament, you chase ideas, decide by feelings, and act on a whim. Through experience you learned to look at facts, judge by logic, and pull things together in order. You worry about someone after correcting them because your structure and your warmth are both at work.
ENFP>ESTJ.yure: Three of four tendencies differ, so your results can change a lot. Picture yourself leading at work and you come out a practical leader; picture yourself having fun with friends and you come out a free-thinking idea person.
ENFP>ESTJ.plus: You can care for someone right after being firm because you have both structure and warmth. A senior who is strict yet kind is a real source of strength for juniors.
ENFP>ESTJ.tip: On days you had to correct someone, try saying "Thanks, that really helped" before you leave. Saying it carries your kindness more directly than checking on them from afar.
ENFP>ESTJ.hidden: You usually value doing things by the book, but your temperament also lets you come up with ideas no one else thinks of. When a routine meeting sparks a thought like "What if we did the opposite?", that's this strength. Say it out loud once, and your team will count on you for new ideas.

ENFP>ESFJ.title: Fresh ideas and careful attention, delivered together.
ENFP>ESFJ.body: "Let's do something different this year!" is usually your line. And on the day, you're quietly making sure no one is left out. Drawing energy from people and deciding with your heart have been the same from birth until now. Your feel for new possibilities and respect for experience, your lightness and your loyalty are all there.
ENFP>ESFJ.say: "I'll book the seats and food. The rest is a surprise!"
ENFP>ESFJ.do: When you hear a friend is feeling down, you go see them that same day.
ENFP>ESFJ.worry: You want everyone to be happy so much that if a new idea gets a lukewarm reaction, you pull it right away. Adventure and the comfort of the usual both matter, and you go back and forth.
ENFP>ESFJ.karai: You planned the surprise, then got nervous and checked with the guest of honor first.
ENFP>ESFJ.aru: You find a new restaurant and suggest it to everyone, but if the response is lukewarm, you quickly say, "Actually, let's just go to the usual place."
ENFP>ESFJ.why: Getting energy from people and deciding by feelings are the core that stayed the same from the start. By temperament, you get excited by new things and move freely in the moment. Through experience you learned to watch people closely and prepare properly. You get stuck between adventure and comfort because you know two ways to make people happy.
ENFP>ESFJ.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on two questions: "New things or familiar things?" and "Do you plan ahead?" When you're busy preparing for an event you come out a caring planner; on a day you wander out for fun you come out a free adventurer.
ENFP>ESFJ.plus: When a thoughtful person suggests something new, everyone feels safe joining in. Seeing others so clearly that you want to back down is actually your strength.
ENFP>ESFJ.tip: Pitch new ideas as "Want to try it just once?" A one-time try is easy for people to say yes to, so you won't feel the need to take it back right away.
ENFP>ESFJ.hidden: You usually prepare things carefully, but your temperament also gives you a lightness that enjoys the unplanned. When someone texts "Can you meet up right now?" and you head out without a second thought and end up laughing hard, that strength is showing. Lean into it, and you'll have more happy surprises in love and friendship.

ENFP>ISTP.title: You try ideas right away, and calmly fix what doesn't work.
ENFP>ISTP.body: Before reading the manual, you take it apart. If it doesn't work, you calmly find the cause and fix it. Adapting flexibly to the moment is the part of you that never wavers. Energy from people and deep focus alone, a feel for possibilities and an eye for facts, a heart for feelings and a head for logic — you have both of each.
ENFP>ISTP.say: "Eh, I'll find out once I try it."
ENFP>ISTP.do: When a friend says their phone is acting up, you fiddle with the settings and fix it on the spot.
ENFP>ISTP.worry: Your waves of wanting fun with people and wanting to work quietly alone are big, and you worry people think you're antisocial. Showing feelings through action is easier than words, so you can be misunderstood.
ENFP>ISTP.karai: You said you'd "just tidy up quickly," and somehow you're rearranging the whole room.
ENFP>ISTP.aru: Your heart says "I get it" when a friend shares a problem, but all that comes out of your mouth is "So why not just do this?"
ENFP>ISTP.why: Being flexible in the moment is the steady part your temperament and character share. By temperament, you get excited with people, chase ideas, and decide by feelings. Through experience you learned to work with your hands alone, look at the facts, and think logically. You show empathy through solutions because you want to help with both heart and logic.
ENFP>ISTP.yure: Three tendencies differ, so your results can change a lot. On a day spent having fun with friends you come out outgoing and feelings-first; on a day absorbed in a solo project you come out quiet and logical, so each result may feel different.
ENFP>ISTP.plus: People remember the one who quietly fixes things and lends a hand. Showing it through action is a real form of empathy too.
ENFP>ISTP.tip: Before offering a fix, add one line: "That sounds really hard." That alone makes your answer land as reliable, not cold.
ENFP>ISTP.hidden: You usually act on the facts in front of you, but your temperament also lets you picture what comes next. When you're scrolling a map on your phone and think, "It'd be fun to go all the way out here," and a trip starts taking shape, that's this strength. Share those daydreams, and you'll find people to chase dreams with at work and in your hobbies.

ENFP>ISFP.title: Loving the laughter of a crowd and the quiet of being alone.
ENFP>ISFP.body: After a big laugh with friends, you slip away to photograph a flower by the road. That's so you. Caring about feelings and following your heart is the part of you that stays the same. Energy from people and comfort alone, imagination for the unseen and a love of the colors, sounds and textures right in front of you — they all live together in you.
ENFP>ISFP.say: "Let's not plan anything today and just wander around."
ENFP>ISFP.do: Even when you're out with friends, you're the one who stops alone to take a photo of a view you love.
ENFP>ISFP.worry: Wanting to connect and wanting to keep your own pace are both strong, so turning down an invite always stings a little. You love so many things, but get stuck when asked about future goals.
ENFP>ISFP.karai: You see a cute outfit and buy it on the spot, with no plans to wear it anywhere.
ENFP>ISFP.aru: You're really happy when a friend says "Let's grab dinner sometime," but once a date is set, it somehow feels a little heavy.
ENFP>ISFP.why: Caring about feelings and going with the flow are steady parts your temperament and character share. By temperament, you get energy from connecting with people and look toward possibilities. Through experience you grew the ability to savor time alone and feel the beauty right in front of you. Invitations make you happy yet plans feel heavy as they get close because you need both time with people and time to rest alone.
ENFP>ISFP.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on two questions: "Do people energize you?" and "Future possibilities or what's in front of you?" Answer with memories of a lively trip and you come out outgoing and idea-driven; picture a solo walk and you come out quiet and sensory.
ENFP>ISFP.plus: You feel down after saying no because you value that connection. People who protect their own pace are the ones who keep good relationships going longer.
ENFP>ISFP.tip: When you say no, add the next plan: "I'll skip this time, but I'd love to go next month." They'll know you still want to see them, so you won't feel down after saying no.
ENFP>ISFP.hidden: You're good at savoring the present, and your temperament also lets you picture an exciting future you haven't seen yet. When you're looking back at trip photos and already imagining several places to go next, that's this strength. Turn those daydreams into small goals, and you'll enjoy answering when someone asks about your future plans.

ENFP>ESTP.title: Off the moment the idea hits, doing the math on the way.
ENFP>ESTP.body: The moment you hear there are no weekend plans, you've picked where to go. People think of you as "the one who always makes something happen." Drawing energy from people and moving with the moment are shared by your temperament and character. With imagination and a grip on reality, heart and a clean cut, you jump in and still weigh what's worth it.
ENFP>ESTP.say: "Anyone free tonight? Let's go get dinner."
ENFP>ESTP.do: A friend sighs "I'm bored," and that same day the two of you are at the new bowling alley.
ENFP>ESTP.worry: After deciding on impulse, you worry whether you left someone's feelings behind. Chasing fun, your prep for what's next always ends up last-minute.
ENFP>ESTP.karai: You walk into a shop "just to look," start chatting with the staff, and walk out having bought something.
ENFP>ESTP.aru: You stop by a place "just for a bit," get carried away, and end up barely catching the last train. The next day, you text a friend, "Did I talk way too much last night?"
ENFP>ESTP.why: Getting energy from people and going with the flow are the foundation your temperament and character share. By temperament, you chase future ideas and decide by feelings. Through experience you learned to grab the chance in front of you and decide quickly with logic. You act on impulse and then want to check on people's feelings because you have both drive and kindness.
ENFP>ESTP.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on two questions: "Facts or possibilities?" and "Logic or feelings?" Picture yourself playing sports or having fun and you come out a practical doer; picture a late night sharing dreams and you come out idea-driven, so you may move between a few types.
ENFP>ESTP.plus: Because you look back after the rush, your energy never leaves people behind. Your ability to move the moment inspiration hits makes everyone's days more fun.
ENFP>ESTP.tip: Before you head out, set a phone alarm for when you want to leave. When it goes off, you'll stop and check the time, so "suddenly it's the last train" happens less.
ENFP>ESTP.hidden: You're a doer who moves fast, but your temperament also lets you see big possibilities in a single moment. When you wander into a shop and think, "It'd be so fun to host an event here," that's this strength. Nurture those sparks on purpose, and you'll create plans that pull people in at work and at play.

ENFP>ESFP.title: A trip around the world and today's crepe — you mean both.
ENFP>ESFP.body: You make people laugh with dreamy stories and still savor today's meal and view. The days of the people with you get a little brighter. Drawing energy from people, caring about feelings and moving with the moment are the parts that never shake. You have both imagination for what's ahead and a love of fun right now.
ENFP>ESFP.do: Walking home with friends, if you spot a festival, you head straight in.
ENFP>ESFP.worry: There's so much fun that money and time always run short. Because you look so cheerful, it's a little lonely when no one notices you're down.
ENFP>ESFP.karai: Every photo comes with "Best moment of the day!"—and you have several of those a day.
ENFP>ESFP.aru: On the way home from passionately talking about traveling the world someday, you impulse-buy a new crepe and some makeup, and your travel fund slips further away.
ENFP>ESFP.why: Getting energy from people, deciding by feelings, and moving freely are the same in your temperament and in your character. The only difference is where you look. By temperament, you dream about possibilities, and through experience you learned to savor the moment. You can be serious about both big dreams and today's fun because your ability to enjoy life is strong.
ENFP>ESFP.yure: Only one tendency differs: future possibilities or present fun. Answer while picturing your dreams and you lean on inspiration; think back to your recent days off and you lean toward enjoying the moment, so you may go back and forth between two types.
ENFP>ESFP.plus: You run short on money because there's so much you can enjoy. People who take both big dreams and today's fun seriously brighten everyone around them.
ENFP>ESFP.tip: On payday, move your dream money into a separate account first. With it set aside, you can spend the rest freely, so you don't have to give up today's fun or your dream.
ENFP>ESFP.hidden: You enjoy the present with everything you've got, but your temperament also lets you spot future possibilities in what people say. When a friend mentions something offhand and you surprise them with "You could totally make that a job!", that strength is at work. Use it on purpose, and you'll be the one who cheers on everyone's dreams.
